title: The Dutch Golden Age
description: Light, intimacy, and virtuosity from the 17th-century Netherlands.

items.title: Aristotle with a Bust of Homer
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt's 1653 oil on canvas depicts the ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle in a moment of contemplative study, his hand resting upon a bust of Homer. The painting showcases Rembrandt's masterful use of light and shadow, highlighting Aristotle's thoughtful expression and the rich textures of his attire.
items.tags: aristotle, homer, philosophy, baroque, dutch golden age, portrait, contemplation, chiaroscuro

items.title: Flora
items.description_narrative: This oil painting by Rembrandt depicts Flora, the Roman goddess of flowers and spring, likely presented in a richly adorned costume. The work exemplifies Rembrandt's mastery of chiaroscuro and psychological depth, characteristic of his mature painting style.
items.tags: portrait, mythology, Dutch Golden Age, Baroque, oil painting, allegorical, expressive

items.title: Portrait of a Man ("The Auctioneer")
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt van Rijn masterfully captures the essence of an individual in this intimate oil portrait, likely depicting an auctioneer. The artist employs rich brushwork and chiaroscuro to highlight the man's thoughtful expression and sturdy presence against a dark background.
items.tags: portrait, man, oil painting, dutch golden age, baroque, somber, realistic, individual

items.title: Herman Doomer (ca. 1595–1650)
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt's 1640 oil on wood portrait captures Herman Doomer, a master cabinetmaker from Amsterdam. The artist employs his signature dramatic lighting and rich brushwork to render the sitter's presence with striking realism and depth.
items.tags: portrait, Dutch Golden Age, oil painting, Baroque, realism, Herman Doomer, 17th century

items.title: Portrait of Gerard de Lairesse
items.description_narrative: This striking portrait by Rembrandt captures Gerard de Lairesse, a fellow artist, with a profound intensity. Executed in oil on canvas, the work exemplifies Rembrandt's mastery of light and psychological depth.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, Dutch Golden Age, Baroque, realism, solemn, Gerard de Lairesse

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.description_narrative: This striking self-portrait by Rembrandt captures the artist in his later years, reflecting on his life with profound introspection. Painted in 1660, it showcases his mastery of light and shadow through rich oil paint.
items.tags: self-portrait, baroque, dutch golden age, oil painting, introspection, masterwork, 17th century

items.title: Hendrickje Stoffels (1626–1663)
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt captures Hendrickje Stoffels, his long-time companion, with remarkable intimacy and psychological depth. His masterful use of light and shadow illuminates her pensive expression, revealing a moment of quiet contemplation.
items.tags: portrait, woman, rembrandt, dutch golden age, oil painting, pensive, intimate

items.title: Bellona
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt's striking 1633 portrait depicts Bellona, the Roman goddess of war, helmeted and armed. Her powerful gaze and commanding presence embody the strength and formidable nature associated with conflict.
items.tags: bellona, goddess, war, portrait, baroque, dutch golden age, commanding, powerful

items.title: A Maid Asleep
items.description_narrative: Johannes Vermeer's 'A Maid Asleep' captures a quiet domestic moment, depicting a maid who has succumbed to slumber at a table. The painting masterfully employs light to illuminate the scene, highlighting textures and creating a serene atmosphere.
items.tags: maid, domestic, interior, sleeping figure, genre painting, Dutch Golden Age, serene, quiet

items.title: Study of a Young Woman
items.description_narrative: Johannes Vermeer's "Study of a Young Woman" captures a pensive figure against a dark background, showcasing his masterful use of light and shadow. This oil on canvas offers a rare glimpse into the artist's exploration of human emotion and form.
items.tags: portrait, figure study, dutch golden age, baroque, oil painting, realism, light, pensive

items.title: Charity
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas by Guido Reni depicts the allegorical figure of Charity, often personified as a mother nurturing her children. The tender poses and soft light reflect Reni's characteristic elegance and his profound influence on Baroque painting.
items.tags: baroque, allegory, classical, mother and child, religious, elegant, painting

items.title: The Crucifixion with the Virgin and Saint John
items.description_narrative: Hendrick ter Brugghen's powerful oil on canvas depicts the solemn scene of the Crucifixion, featuring the Virgin Mary and Saint John at the foot of the cross. This deeply moving work exemplifies the artist's distinctive style, combining dramatic lighting with profound emotional intensity.
items.tags: religious, crucifixion, baroque, dutch, oil painting, sacred, somber, caravaggism

items.title: The Jabach Family
items.description_narrative: Charles Le Brun's 'The Jabach Family' grandly portrays the prominent banker Everhard Jabach with his family, reflecting their status and the artistic tastes of the era. This large-scale oil painting exemplifies the formal grandeur and detailed portraiture characteristic of 17th-century French art.
items.tags: family portrait, baroque, french art, 17th century, formal, le brun, oil painting

items.title: The Fieschi Morgan Staurotheke
items.medium: Gilded silver, gold, enamel worked in cloisonné, and niello
items.description_narrative: This magnificent staurotheke, a reliquary for a fragment of the True Cross, exemplifies the exquisite craftsmanship of the early 9th century Byzantine Empire. Fashioned from gilded silver, gold, and intricate cloisonné enamel, it showcases the era's dedication to sacred art and precious materials.
items.tags: byzantine, reliquary, metalwork, gold, enamel, early medieval, religious

items.title: Portrait of a Woman, Possibly a Nun of San Secondo; (verso) Scene in Grisaille
items.medium: Oil on wood; (verso: oil and gold on wood)
items.description_narrative: This intimate oil on wood portrait, likely depicting a nun from San Secondo, was created by Jacometto Veneziano between approximately 1485 and 1495. The reverse of the panel features a grisaille scene, showcasing the artist's versatility with oil and gold on wood.
items.tags: portrait, Renaissance, oil painting, grisaille, religious, Italian, detailed

items.title: Portrait of Alvise Contarini(?); (verso) A Tethered Roebuck
items.medium: Oil on wood; verso: oil and gold on wood
items.description_narrative: This double-sided artwork presents a potential portrait of Alvise Contarini on one panel, meticulously rendered in oil on wood. The verso reveals a detailed depiction of a tethered roebuck, executed in oil and gold on wood.
items.tags: portrait, Renaissance, Venetian, oil painting, animal, wood panel, double-sided

items.title: Young Man and Woman in an Inn
items.description_narrative: Frans Hals's "Young Man and Woman in an Inn" depicts a spirited interaction between two figures within a common setting. Painted in 1623, this oil on canvas work exemplifies a genre scene from the artist's prolific output.
items.tags: dutch golden age, genre scene, portraiture, inn, young couple, baroque, lively

items.title: Boy with a Lute
items.description_narrative: Frans Hals captures a lively young boy engaged with his lute, suggesting either a portrait or a genre scene of music-making. The artist's distinctive loose brushwork and spontaneous style bring a sense of immediacy and vitality to the subject.
items.tags: boy, lute, music, portraiture, dutch golden age, baroque, vitality

items.title: Petrus Scriverius (1576–1660)
items.description_narrative: This oil on wood painting by Frans Hals depicts the Dutch scholar and historian Petrus Scriverius. Hals captures Scriverius with characteristic directness and lively brushwork, reflecting his mastery of portraiture during the Dutch Golden Age.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, Dutch Golden Age, Baroque, realism, individual, scholar

items.title: Jacob Willemsz van Veen (1456–1535), the Artist's Father
items.description_narrative: This solemn portrait depicts Jacob Willemsz van Veen, the father of artist Maarten van Heemskerck. Executed in oil on wood in 1532, it offers a realistic portrayal of the subject.
items.tags: portrait, father, realism, renaissance, dutch art, oil painting, male portrait
